newsitem.title: FRENCH POLYNESIA: Idyllic Polynesian island for sale.
newsitem.headline: Idyllic Polynesian island for sale.

text.p: An idyllic island in French Polynesia, whose beaches have been enjoyed by Brigitte Bardot and Princess Caroline of Monaco, will go to auction next month, a newspaper said on Friday.
Tupai atoll, a 1,000 hectare (2,500 acre) paradise reputed to be one of most beautiful islands of the Tahiti archipelago, goes under the hammer on October 30, the daily Les Nouvelles de Tahiti said.

It will be sold in two separate lots, one of 700 hectares (1,750 acres) at a starting price of 82.5 million francs ($16.4 million) and the other of 300 hectares (750 acres) at 33 million francs ($6.6 million).

Owned for several decades by a solicitor now forced to give it up because of financial difficulties, Tupai features a small airstrip which has helped make its remote, unspoiled beaches a popular holiday paradise for screen stars and royalty.
Legend says that mutinous Chilean pirates who stole riches from the Peruvian coast buried their treasure there in 1822.
Several search operations in the final years of the 19th century failed to unearth the hidden treasure, but the mystery is likely to push up the atoll's sale price.
Film legend Marlon Brando owns another island near Tahiti, Tetiaroa, where he has built a small hotel and lives as a recluse.
